data.why: The old shelter layout on the lawn; the rain is followed from the roof to the ground, the slabs, the low edge, the gutter and into a rain barrel, with a leaf riding along. The camera stays on the shelter and steps to the gutter and the barrel at the end.

chain.shows: the wind tips the shelter up
the dug ground under it turns to mud
rain blows in sideways over the slabs
rain pours off the roof behind the wall
the spout digs a hole in the lawn

surprises.claim: Concrete footings anchor a shelter's posts against wind uplift.
surprises.search: concrete footings anchor posts wind uplift pergola

surprises.claim: Paving slabs are laid on a compacted sub-base so they stay level.
surprises.search: paving slabs compacted sub-base stay level

surprises.claim: A gutter collects roof runoff and sends it to a downspout.
A rain barrel under a downspout stores roof water for the garden.
surprises.search: rain barrel under downspout stores rainwater for garden

ideas.idea: four posts and a roof appear on the lawn
wind hits it and the shelter tips up on one side
the shelter settles back, a trench is dug and concrete footings grow under the posts
rain falls and muddy puddles spread under the roof
a floor of paving slabs wipes in under the roof
wind and rain spray blow in sideways across the floor
a back wall and a side wall appear and the spray stops
a garden shelter: a roof on anchored posts with a floor and walls
rain pours off the roof's low edge onto the ground
a gutter and spout appear along the low edge
water from the spout splashes a muddy hole in the lawn
a rain barrel catches the water from the spout
the rain stops; stepping stones lead to the dry shelter
the finished shelter stands calm in the sun

sentences.text: If you stand four posts under a roof, you have a garden shelter.
But wind catches the roof and tips it over.
So you pour concrete footings under the posts.
But rain turns the dug ground into mud.
So you lay paving slabs on top.
But wind blows the rain sideways across the slabs.
So you add a back and a side wall.
But behind the back wall, rain pours off the roof.
So you hang a gutter along the low edge.
But the spout digs a hole in the lawn.
So a barrel under the spout saves it.
Now sit under four dry posts and a roof.
Congratulations, you have built a garden shelter.
